solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: B (fairness above all) is the main trap but is an overstatement; distractor set is otherwise weak (A contradicts 'valuable', D unsupported)
minor: key paraphrases paragraph 2's list (uncertainty, fairness) closely, and items 03/08 also rehearse that list
R015-01.notes: 'Only half true' = time matters, but how the wait feels (uncertainty, fairness, etc.) matters at least as much (P2). B overstates; A, D unsupported.

flags: minor: A nearly restates the critics' theme-park sentence ('more bearable without making it any shorter'), so this is close to a direct analogy
R015-02.notes: Airport kept total time about the same but changed how it felt; critics say such moves manage perception without fixing the real problem. B contradicts 'stayed about the same'; C reverses critics' view; D unsupported.

R015-03.notes: Posted estimates make the wait's length known, so they address uncertainty (P2: uncertain waits feel longer than waits of known length).

flags: minor: D echoes passage wording ('advances a little at a time' / 'advances a few steps')
R015-04.notes: P6: steady movement and a good ending outweigh total length. D is steady to the end despite being longer. A (stall then sudden empty) mirrors the 'stalls and then lurches' line and tempts students focused on the quick ending; B ends badly; C is erratic.

R015-05.notes: Contrasted with steady advance after a stall, 'lurches forward' = moves suddenly and unevenly. B is the off-context dictionary sense; A and D contradict 'forward' and the contrast.

R015-06.notes: The author says the old assumption 'turned out to be only half true', calls the applications 'most cited' and a finding 'most intriguing', and lays out the critics vs. defenders debate. So A. D (neutral) tempts students because the author mostly reports, but the evaluative wording rules it out. B and C are extreme.

R015-07.notes: The preceding 'story we tell ourselves afterward' means designers shape the remembered experience. A and C are literal readings of 'authors'; D's 'alone decide' is extreme and misses the point about memory.

flags: minor: overlaps with R015-03 and R015-01; all three rehearse the P2 list, and C ('told exactly how long') reverses the R015-03 key, so the items reinforce each other
R015-08.notes: P2: a wait that seems unfair (a later arrival served first) feels longer. B, C and D each reverse a P2 claim.
